crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience covers the qualitative and mixed methods work of turning interviews, diaries, focus groups and open survey answers into themes, codes and narratives. It sits between close reading and computational text analysis, and it is used in social science, health services research, education and human computer interaction. The aim is not to count opinions but to describe how people make sense of their circumstances, and to show where those accounts converge or diverge.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on transcripts, audio recordings, field notes and coded excerpts, usually held in a qualitative data analysis package such as NVivo, ATLAS.ti, MAXQDA or Dedoose, or in a shared spreadsheet for smaller studies. Machine assistance comes from transcription services, topic models, embedding based clustering and large language models used for first pass coding.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical study moves through sampling, data collection, transcription, open coding, constant comparison and theme development, with memo writing running alongside. Mixed methods designs add a quantitative strand, often a survey or a coded count, and then integrate the two at the interpretation stage rather than the analysis stage. When models are used, the usual pattern is machine suggestion followed by human review, with disagreements logged and resolved by discussion among coders.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Consent, anonymity and the risk of re-identification matter more here than in most text work, because verbatim quotes can expose a participant even when names are removed. Ethics review, data sharing agreements and restrictions on moving sensitive transcripts to third party services shape what tools are usable. Provenance is tracked through codebooks, audit trails and versioned transcripts, and any claim drawn from a paper should point to the original work rather than to a search summary.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward hybrid workflows where models handle transcription, first pass coding and pattern surfacing, and researchers spend their time on interpretation and reflexivity. That shift raises questions about how much of the analytic chain can be documented when a model's output is not reproducible, and about whether saturation still means what it did. Expect more attention to reporting standards for machine assisted qualitative work and to methods for validating themes against the underlying accounts.
